clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old male presented with right upper limb numbness, focal seizures, and left parietal lobe hypodensity on CT, initially suspected as stroke with secondary epilepsy. Positive Spirometra mansoni IgG serology confirmed parasitic infection. Brain MRI revealed a left parietal lobe lesion with edema suggestive of inflammation or parasitic involvement. CSF studies were mostly normal. The patient underwent praziquantel treatment across multiple hospital stays, resulting in serology negativity and MRI lesion changes consistent with partial resolution. Seizure control and symptomatic treatment were also administered. Although detailed neurological follow-up findings are not documented, the clinical course, treatment response, serological conversion, and imaging evolution support the diagnosis of a CNS Spirometra mansoni infection.
